test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 02 Sept, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of the following, set up in June 1986, is responsible for the management of civil aerodromes and civil enclaves as well as for maintenance and operation of aeronautical communication systems at all the airports?
solution:
The correct answer is __**National Airports Authority**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **National Airports Authority (NAA)** was established in June 1986 under the National Airports Authority Act, 1985.
 
• The NAA was responsible for the management of **civil aerodromes and civil enclaves** across India.
 
• It was also tasked with the maintenance and operation of **aeronautical communication systems** at all airports in the country.
 
• Later, the National Airports Authority merged with the International Airports Authority of India in 1995 to form the **Airports Authority of India (AAI)**.
 
• This merger aimed to improve efficiency in airport management and streamline operations across all civil aviation facilities in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Delhi International Airport Limited (DIAL)**:

 
 
• DIAL is a joint venture consortium established to manage and operate the Indira Gandhi International Airport in Delhi.
 
• It is a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) between the Airports Authority of India, GMR Group, and other stakeholders.
 
• DIAL focuses on modernization and efficient management of Delhi Airport but is not responsible for other civil aerodromes in India.
 
 
 
• **Airports Authority of India (AAI)**:
 
 
• AAI was formed in 1995 after the merger of the National Airports Authority (NAA) and the International Airports Authority of India (IAAI).
 
• It is responsible for managing and operating airports, providing air navigation services, and ensuring the development and modernization of civil aviation infrastructure in India.
 
• AAI oversees more than 100 airports in India, including both domestic and international airports.
 
 
 
• **Airports Council International (ACI)**:
 
 
• ACI is a global organization representing the world’s airports.
 
• It provides a platform for airport operators to exchange best practices, promote airport excellence, and advocate for policies benefiting the aviation industry.
 
• However, ACI is not directly involved in managing or operating airports.
